mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 0.34% is at a historically low level, indicating an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPI) exceeds 3.0% year-over-year, it signals persistent inflation that prompts central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0% and the federal funds rate remains below 0.5%, the market perceives a 'sticky inflation' scenario that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to delayed policy response.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a 'sticky inflation' regime (defined by CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5), the S&P 500 tends to have negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to market concerns about prolonged inflation and delayed rate cuts.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-demand regime (defined by GDPC1 growth below 1% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to have negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings growth and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 1% annualized, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0 and housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1100.0, the combined weakness in manufacturing and housing signals a broad economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0 and HOUST < 1100.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 persons signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS falls by more than 50 (thousands) in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
